text:
**Rounds 25 to 30, 15 to 19 November: names, washes, triggers, SHAME, Meaning, Stress, status** *(2026-11-19)*:

> I think that for the larger-than-life needs, we're going to go with respect and compassion.

> The reason I wanted to switch to competence is because of its interaction with identifiably competent.

> Yes, pain, thirst, itch, and air all join the body band.

> nothing is necessary and everything is sufficient

> Attention isn't a picking of a given feature. It is any organizational schema that can be held in mind.

> I think competence is correct still, but I agree that present is not correct.

> I think it's a floor that's defended, no ceiling, and that floor itself is your set point that raises over time.

> Like, these needs aren't independent.

*Curator's messages in the project's theory and analyst thread: 15 November 2026, 21:46 PST (Round 25); 16 November, 07:43 PST (Round 26); 16 November, 15:39 PST, re-sent complete at 17:24 (Round 27); 18 November (Round 28); 19 November, 06:30 PT (Round 29) and 11:32 PT (Round 30); filed {FILED}. Quoted verbatim in separate excerpts, each contiguous.*

After the later rounds of 15 November filed above, the theory thread ran six more with the curator. The rows below (G305 to G318) carry what they changed, each marked as his ruling, his statement or the analyst's proposal. The needs' names now stand as follows.

| Need | Name now | Earlier names in these files | Name ruled |
|---|---|---|---|
| First | Competence | Knowledge | 2026-11-19 (Round 29) |
| Second | Meaning | Nest | 2026-11-18 (Round 28) |
| Third | Belonging | Belonging | unchanged |
| Fourth | Respect | being visibly respectable | 2026-11-19 (Round 30) |
| Fifth | Compassion | being visibly compassionate | 2026-11-19 (Round 30) |
| Sixth | the body | the body | unchanged |

Older rows keep the older names as history; the rows below carry the rest.

text:
| **G305** | The needs' current names: Competence (was Knowledge; definition unchanged, confidence in the map and in the plans), Meaning (was Nest; definition unchanged, how predictably good the things and people that carry one's models are), Belonging, Respect and Compassion (were being visibly respectable and being visibly compassionate), and the body; older rows keep the older names as history (renames G266 to G269 and G295) | **OPEN as to structure; the names are the curator's rulings: Meaning 2026-11-18 (Round 28), Competence 2026-11-19 (Round 29), Respect and Compassion 2026-11-19 (Round 30: "So respect and compassion are actually, I think, great decisions. I'm open to alternatives.").** His sentence on PANIC/GRIEF, "panic grief just really needs to be sadness" (2026-11-19, Round 30), is entered as his and taken as a rename awaiting his confirmation; the thread has put it to him, and no row is renamed for it. No evidence bears on a name |
| **G306** | The body band holds seven: Warmth, Food, Sleep, pain, thirst, itch and air; pain may be a missing set point that "would probably grow into sadness more than anything"; the safety tag of the event stories sits under the body ("I'll accept your calling of safety as a body trigger.") (extends G266) | **OPEN. The band is the curator's ruling (2026-11-16, Round 26, with no new cards); the safety placement is his ruling (2026-11-18, Round 28) on the analyst's question.** No project measurement of the four new members |
| **G307** | The four washes after Rounds 25 to 28: dopamine marks a sudden rise in the whole chain's confidence, with no threshold ("The full chain, top to bottom."), and is also the go signal; norepinephrine is the temperature of the swap and not of the walk, a booster and not the swap ("yes, it's just a booster. That's fine. It's temperature."); acetylcholine is orthogonal to attention ("Acetylcholine is orthogonal.") and closed ("Okay, so acetylcholine satisfied."); serotonin is stay the course plus rank, with shedding given to dream sleep; the washes are levels and not switches ("it's four separate levels") (settles the amendments of G299) | **OPEN, provisional by his word (he is "not really set" on them, G299); the seats are the curator's rulings: dopamine 2026-11-15 (Round 25) and 2026-11-16 (Round 27, the go signal); norepinephrine the same two dates; acetylcholine 2026-11-16 (Rounds 26 and 27); serotonin 2026-11-18 (Round 28).** G299's amendments on dopamine and norepinephrine are now his; the one tying acetylcholine to attention is declined; serotonin as not one number is not ruled on. Nothing in it is read from text. No project measurement |
| **G308** | Triggers are graded and no single feature is required ("nothing is necessary and everything is sufficient"); set points stay, and schemas and learned cues forecast them ("Set points forecast by schemas. I agree with that."); guilt and pride stay labels and are out of the channel tests ("they're just not part of this party") (refines G271) | **OPEN. The curator's rulings (2026-11-18, Round 28).** No project measurement bears on the grading as such |
| **G309** | RAGE fires on a sudden drop ("A sudden drop in anything"), and blame is something RAGE does and not what fires it; the status check, which tilts a sudden drop toward RAGE for the bigger one and toward FEAR for the smaller one, is a later check on RAGE and FEAR and not the whole difference ("Agreed on number four."); RAGE narrows inference onto the person who caused the problem and dives into that person's vulnerabilities ("It needs a vulnerability."); RAGE and FEAR may be separate and fire together (refines G273 and G279) | **OPEN. The trigger, blame and status-check clauses are the curator's rulings (2026-11-18, Round 28); the narrowing is his refinement (2026-11-19, Round 29) and the vulnerabilities his statement (Round 30), not ruled on; RAGE and FEAR as separate is his statement, not ruled on (Round 29: "I thought Rage and Fear had similar looking triggers, and I didn't think they could fire together.").** The analyst's limit, not ruled on: measured thinking about the target of anger is cruder, not deeper (anger narrows attentional scope; lit, abstract: doi 10.1037/a0039226). The published trigger tables build blame into anger, which he reads as "blending in the trigger with the outcome". Tests: lattice LD2 and LB2 (proposed) |
| **G310** | A moment is a profile over the nine channels and not one label: several fire at once, each weighted by how well the moment fits its trigger; there are no general brakes, and PLAY turns itself off ("I think that might be a special case for play."), keyed to a lot of FEAR ("It requires a lot of play and fear for them to inhibit each other."); attention is a transformation over the features of a moment, a schema, and not a weight on single features ("really what you're looking at is a transformation on top of the features"); attending biases the weightings ("all you're doing is biasing the weightings by attending to a particular part."); a channel cannot be put on directly, and what looks like that is a fluency ("those are all fluencies") (refines G271, G277 and G284) | **OPEN. The profile is the curator's ruling (2026-11-19, Round 29); no general brakes and attention as a transformation are his rulings on the analyst's equation (Round 30); the biasing and the fluency reading are his (Round 29), the second withdrawing the analyst's body-as-handle proposal.** He does not mean PCA as such ("I don't think I meant PCA"); the analyst's note, not ruled on, is that the claim needs strengths that cannot go below zero and may rise together. Test: lattice LT1 (proposed) |
| **G311** | SHAME's working trigger is a decrease in competence, and someone present is not required ("You can feel self-shame, I guess."), replacing the Round 29 working wording, a decrease in competence with someone else present; shame occurs when a person breaks an identity, and moral failures are identity failures ("so shame occurs when you break your identities"; "Moral failures are identity failures."; "Heuristics do not inherently provide shame"); embarrassment is a different thing from shame ("shame and embarrassment are going to be different things."), shame with a little PLAY, and is out of SHAME's stand-ins; guilt and shame are treated as kind of the same thing ("I've treated them as kind of the same thing.") (refines G274) | **OPEN. The trigger is the curator's ruling (2026-11-19, Round 30); embarrassment as a different thing is his ruling (Round 29), and its makeup he holds against the analyst's disagreement (Round 30); guilt with shame answers in part the thread's question on guilt's home (Round 30); shame on breaking an identity is his statement, not ruled on (Round 30).** Many shame events happen alone (lit, abstract: doi 10.1037/0022-3514.70.6.1256). The analyst's limit on embarrassment, not accepted by him: comparing studies put it further from shame and from amusement. Test: lattice LD1 (proposed) |
| **G312** | Each feeling word is kept as a best guess at its mix of channels, with a central cultural mix per word and a person's error around it; first entries: embarrassed, SHAME with a little PLAY (his); anxious, FEAR with predicted grief ("When people say anxiety, they also mean predicted grief."; his, open); hope, SEEKING plus something ("it's more like seeking plus something else."; his, open), with enthusiasm as SEEKING's hallmark ("what we want is enthusiasm."); contempt's expression goes with SHAME ("The expression of contempt goes with the channel of shame"; his, open); a nervous laugh is the ask ("It's the ask."; his); a learned fluency that is not a channel is a custom fluency ("custom fluency. That'll do it."), and on his account channels are fluencies too (extends G270) | **OPEN, untested. Keeping the table is the curator's instruction (2026-11-19, Round 30); the term custom fluency is his ruling (Round 30); the entries are his statements of Round 30, not ruled on.** On contempt this returns to his Round 15 reading, the sender's side of shame, which his Round 16 reading (a stored low reading that sets DISGUST off) and Round 17 reading (a level left by anger, as in G279) had replaced. His Round 29 sentence against nervous laughter was a transcription error by his own correction. His limit on anxious: one point of evidence and a feeling from expertise. Test: lattice LD4 (proposed) |
| **G313** | Meaning is a floor that is defended, with no ceiling, and the floor rises over a life ("It's a one-directional set point"); it is never traded away by choice ("people will trade other things for it but not it for other things"), and what is traded when a sacred value is traded is an indicator ("that's not them trading meaning, that's them trading the indicators for meaning") (refines G268; bears on G291) | **OPEN. The shape and the indicator reading are the curator's rulings (2026-11-19, Round 30), answering the thread's question and the analyst's disagreement; never traded is his statement (Round 29).** Sacred values are traded when the trade is reframed (lit, abstract: doi 10.1016/s1364-6613(03)00135-9), which on his reading trades an indicator. No project measurement |
| **G314** | Stress keeps three states, free, bound and resolved ("We've still got our three."), and schemas bind nothing ("schemas don't bind and can't bind anything"); in Round 30 the curator added that Stress can also be bound by a fluency of any kind ("I think you can also bind it by a fluency of any kind."), which sits against his Round 29 sentence and which the thread has put to him; he draws Stress as the last gauge under the needs, fed by every need's error ("it's the final piece of the chain"), with leftover activation noise going back into the Toolbox ("and that arrow is just leftover activation noise, basically."); and what stresses may be the error on identities, the predictions of the needs ("what actually stresses us out are not errors on needs, but rather errors on the top levels of your identity, on your predictions on those needs.") (refines G281) | **OPEN. The three states (2026-11-16, Round 26) and schemas binding nothing (2026-11-19, Round 29) are the curator's; the three Round 30 items are his statements (2026-11-19), not ruled on.** The last gauge returns to the list of 11 November, where Stress stood among the needs, which Rounds 16 and 17 superseded; it now stands there as the collected error of the others. No project measurement |
| **G315** | Status is relative competence ("status isn't status. It's relative competence on the competence ladder."); competence is the hidden variable, and dominance and prestige are its two indicators: dominance is a fluency for competence, its packaging ("Dominance is instead your fluency for competence."; "I don't think dominance is intimidation."), and prestige is a record of evidence ("Prestige is a record of previous examples of competence."); each need has an identity that tracks it ("needs would all, like I said, have an identity that tracks them."), and the simpler needs have first-order fluencies where Meaning has none (refines G269 and G295) | **OPEN. The curator's statements (status as relative competence, 2026-11-19, Round 29; the indicators and the tracking identities, Round 30), not ruled on.** The analyst's limit (Round 29), not ruled on: the read can part from the thing, so Respect stays a need of its own. On dominance the literature uses one word for two things: a second road to rank by intimidation (lit, abstract: doi 10.1037/a0030398), which he does not mean, and trait dominance that wins influence by signalling competence (lit, abstract: doi 10.1037/a0014201), which is his reading. His point that people cannot see their needs, so status is not in their reports (Round 30), bears on diary tests of rank |
| **G316** | LUST's proposed triggers are five: a change or a slope in status, or a mismatch between one's read of someone's status and society's read; the sense that no one else would love them as one does ("No one would love them like I do, is a real effect."); a large relative competence; boredom ("Being bored explicitly would be a trigger for lust, I bet."); and a lack of meaning ("lacking meaning in life would be something that would trigger lust."); LUST rides in when other channels fire, CARE excepted ("it's always present when other channels are firing"; "Lust can use care, but care doesn't bring lust."), and it inhibits DISGUST (refines G278) | **OPEN, untested. The curator's statements (the triggers, 2026-11-19, Round 29; riding in, Round 30), not ruled on; he asks for a dataset from sex research.** Eight attempts to repeat small laboratory effects of mating cues failed (lit, abstract: Shanks et al., 2015). Test: lattice LB1 (proposed) |
| **G317** | The needs are not independent ("it implies there's a structure that we have not identified, and it bothers me a great deal.") (bears on G266) | **OPEN. The curator's statement (2026-11-19, Round 30), given to the theory thread to decide ("I'm kicking it over to you to decide."); the thread's answer is in its Round 30 walk and is not entered here until he rules.** No project measurement |
| **G318** | Further statements of the curator on 19 November (Round 30), kept so that they are not lost: DISGUST grows out of identity about the body ("I'm someone who doesn't eat vomit") and needs no agent ("I agree, disgust needs no agent."); SHAME's shutting-out "reads an awful lot like self-directed disgust."; in CARE, "Mirroring is part of care, and the person you're mirroring is often crying because they're using the grief network."; joy and PLAY are unsettled ("Joy can't just be play."); reports of rank are held down by a penalty for claiming it ("you're aware that reporting higher status has a penalty"); Compassion cannot be gamed the way Respect can ("you won't really lie about how compassionate you are in the way that you'll lie about how respectable you are."); the split between mastery and competitiveness is competence against dominance ("I think we're seeing the split between competence and dominance that I described earlier."); rumination is noise re-compressing through Stress ("that noise keeps re-compressing into annoyingly the same solutions"; "because it's being looped back through stress."); surprise may fall out of compression ("doesn't surprise technically fall out of compression slightly."); the carry-over of a feeling from one moment to the next may be a reconvergence and not a leftover ("I think what we're seeing with step 9 is a kind of a reconvergence into that shape."; "this is worth checking."; step 9 is the carry-over term of the analyst's equation walk); people differ in HEXACO terms ("It's going to be in Hexaco.") and in "relative willingness to weight the various needs"; reading a person may take two contextual lenses ("can we maybe take something like voice and view the emotional layer as one contextual lens"); and Capital "just kind of refers to autonomy." (bears on G270 to G279, G281 and G283) | **OPEN. The curator's statements (2026-11-19, Round 30), none ruled on.** The thread's answers are in its Round 30 walk and are not entered here until he rules. No project measurement |

His further statements of 19 November are kept in one row (G318). The thread's evidence ledger (238 results keyed to 23 claims) and Theory Book exist as of 19 November in the project record; the repository's card RC1 (lattice packet of 19 November, section 3.9) is to file `results/EVIDENCE_LEDGER.jsonl` and `docs/theory/CLAIM_IDS.json`, rewording no theory row.
